test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

They have built a new bridge across the river.

options.text: A new bridge will have been built across the river by them.
They have been building a new bridge across the river.
A new bridge has been building across the river by them.
A new bridge has been built across the river by them.

solution:
The correct answer is '**A new bridge has been built across the river by them.**'

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Converting a sentence from active to passive voice involves rearranging the sentence so that the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence, and the subject of the active sentence (doer of the action) is typically introduced with "by."
 
• The given sentence is in the present perfect tense, indicated by "**have built**."
 
• The correct passive voice structure for a sentence in the present perfect tense is "**has/have been + past participle of the main verb.**"
 
• Since "**a new bridge**" is singular, we use "**has been**" followed by the past participle "**built**" to accurately convert the statement into passive voice.
 
• The passive voice sentence that retains the original verb tense and meaning without altering important details is "**A new bridge has been built across the river by them.**"

Therefore, the correct answer is ‘**Option 4**’.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 ("**A new bridge will have been built across the river by them.**") unnecessarily changes the tense to the future perfect, altering the time frame suggested by the original sentence.
 
• Option 2 ("**They have been building a new bridge across the river.**") remains in active voice and focuses on the ongoing action rather than the completion, thus not properly converting the sentence to passive voice.
 
• Option 3 ("**A new bridge has been building across the river by them.**") is grammatically incorrect; the correct phrase is "has been built," not "has been building," to correctly form the passive voice.
